g.text: Heuristic watermarks and skew — one guess, swept
watermark = max event time seen so far − skew bound (here 60s)
every value is one subtraction; the only judgement in it is the skew bound
Nothing here measures anything. The 60s is an assumption about how out-of-order the input can be.
Note the stalls: the value repeats whenever an arriving event's time is below the max already seen — the watermark is driven by the maximum, not
Step 1/4 — the heuristic is one line: max seen, minus a guess
The whole heuristic is `max(seen) − skew`. The max is free and exact; the skew is a number a human chose. So every watermark in this book is one
measured quantity minus one guess, and the next two steps are about what happens when the guess is too small or too large.
Heuristic watermarks and skew — one guess, swept
A SWEEP OVER THE SKEW BOUND
what each skew bound does to window [12:00, 12:02) — true sum 19
At skew 0s the pipeline calls 2 events late; at 141s it calls none late and is correct.
Nothing about the DATA changed between those rows. "Late" is a verdict the watermark passes, not a property of an event.
Step 2/4 — too FAST: the guess is small, so real events look late
Read the last column down the table: 2, 1, 1, 0, then 0. The same 9 events, the same arrival times, and the number of "late" events falls from 2
to 0 purely because a configured bound grew. An over-eager watermark does not detect lateness — it creates it.
Heuristic watermarks and skew — one guess, swept
THE EXACT THRESHOLD, AND WHAT IT COSTS
one second of configuration separates the first two rows
296s later than the 60s default, for every window
230s — NOT the threshold, and much larger
The threshold is 141s because the watermark only has to stay below the WINDOW END (12:02) until id 7 lands — it never has to reach back to
So it is derived from 12:04:20 − 12:02: the highest event time seen before the straggler, minus the window's end. Not from the straggler's skew.
Step 3/4 — too SLOW: correct, and the answer arrives much later
The number a reader expects here is 230s — the straggler's skew. The actual threshold is 141s, and the derivation is in the note: the watermark
only needs to stay below the window's END, not below the late event's event time. Worth knowing, because tuning skew to your worst observed delay
Heuristic watermarks and skew — one guess, swept
ONE WATERMARK PER SOURCE, THEN THE MINIMUM
two sources, two watermarks, one safe claim
12:03:20 — it cannot claim more than its least-complete input
a single GLOBAL watermark would say
12:08:00 — 280s more completeness than source "b" can back
Per-source is SAFER and slower: windows [12:02, 12:04), [12:04, 12:06) would close under the global watermark and stay open under the minimum.
That is the cost of the correct answer here — 11 + 7 withheld because an idle source cannot vouch for it.
Step 4/4 — and per-source tracking beats one global guess
Tracking per source means one idle source holds the whole stage back — source "b" stops at 12:03:20 while "a" reaches 12:08:00, and the stage must
claim the lower. That is correct and it costs 2 window's output (11, 7). Real systems add idleness detection precisely to escape this, and that is
a decision to declare a source finished.
